title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (execution record: temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, failure diagnosis, artifact-grounded reproducibility guidance, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational correctness in such workflows depends on produced configurations satisfying deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, ordering/workflow constraints, and safety-group constraints). Prior work has prototyped intent→configuration translation and suggested verifier-integrated generator pipelines but supplies limited artifact-grounded evidence quantifying how verifier-based guardrails change deterministic-invariant compliance under a tightly controlled experimental design [1],[2].

We preregistered study CAND-2026-001 to address a narrowly scoped research question that isolates the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered automated repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Research question (preregistered): under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does permitting at most one verifier-triggered automated repair improve the per-task rate at which a deterministic verifier accepts generated configurations? The paired design therefore measures a repair-only effect on the identical initial candidate; it does not measure effects of constrained prompting, multi-sample generation, or independent first-pass generations.

Contributions. (1) A preregistered, fully archived paired experiment (CAND-2026-001) executing 200 intent→configuration tasks with a deterministic verifier and a hosted LLM (gpt-5-mini) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Complete execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation showing 200 shared initial generations and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). (3) Artifact-grounded confirmatory analysis: baseline pass 199/200, guarded pass 200/200, contingency table (n11=199,n10=1,n01=0,n00=0), paired risk difference 0.005, exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0, bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). (4) A focused failure diagnosis: the single repaired case involved a multi-device ordering violation that the repair corrected deterministically. (5) Reproducibility guidance and bounded interpretation consistent with the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work:
The supplied literature documents active work on intent-driven configuration synthesis and prototype evaluation pipelines for NetOps, and it advocates verifier-integrated generator patterns [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain generate→validate→repair approaches (program repair, test-in-the-loop LLM repair, tool-augmented agents) motivate guarded pipelines as a practical design pattern; however, empirical demonstrations that quantify verifier-acceptance improvements in NetOps are limited in the surveyed set [4],[5]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM safety emphasize failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and recommend verifier gates and provenance recording for operational workflows [6],[7].

Relation to our study. Unlike prior multi-model benchmark work that reports aggregate accuracy on curated question banks, this paper reports a preregistered paired measurement under shared_initial_candidate semantics. That design explicitly isolates the verifier/repair marginal effect on an identical initial candidate and therefore differs from studies comparing independent first-pass generations, constrained prompts, or multiple-sample strategies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as CAND-2026-001 before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, defined as the per-pair difference in the binary event that the deterministic verifier accepts the candidate (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded episodes), allowed at most one automated repair call per task, and declared one confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar). The preregistration and its SHA-256 are archived in the execution bundle.

Task bank and deterministic sampling. We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce 200 tasks sampled from very_hard and extreme workflow patterns (multi-device ordering constraints and dependency rules). The sampling rule was fixed and deterministic (see task_manifest.jsonl). Each task manifest encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and workflow policies. Inclusion/exclusion rules (token-normalized leakage checks, syntactic pre-checks) were applied deterministically prior to any model calls; no preregistered exclusions occurred.

Model configuration and generation semantics. The declared hosted model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini and the manifest records model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial + 1 repair). The recorded model configuration field temperature = null (unset); we explicitly note that null/unset is archived metadata and is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0. Per the preregistration, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1 and maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; the adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics, deterministically reusing the single sampled initial candidate for both baseline and guarded episodes.

Deterministic verifier and scoring. The binary outcome per task was computed by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The verifier performs deterministic syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, ordering/required_sequence conformance, group-level invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up), and other dependency rules specified in each task manifest. The confirmatory scoring rule was full_intent_constraint_validation: an episode scores 1 iff all required invariants pass; otherwise 0. Validator traces (validation_before/validation_after), violation codes, and normalized final configurations are archived for every episode.

Statistical test reproducibility detail. The exact two-sided McNemar p-value reported by the analysis executor is computed from the binomial distribution of discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) under the null that each discordant outcome is equally likely (p = 0.5). Concretely, the two-sided p sums binomial-tail probabilities of discordant counts at least as extreme as the observed outcome under Binomial(n, 0.5). With observed discordants n = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0), the analysis executor reports p = 1.0; the analysis artifacts include the contingency counts and the p-value.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and deterministic reconciliation. The execution manifest records: started_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and completed_at_utc = 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00. Planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 201. Deterministic_reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and consistent pair accounting. Provider-call stage counts: shared_initial_generation = 200; repair = 1; hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 (no cached responses).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Analysis/condition_summary.csv reports:
- Baseline: successes = 199, failures = 1, observed = 200, success_rate = 0.995.
- Guarded: successes = 200, failures = 0, observed = 200, success_rate = 1.000.
Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Statistical inference and interval estimation. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test (analysis executor: exact_mcnemar_two_sided) yields p = 1.0 for the observed discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference was computed using 10,000 resamples with bootstrap_seed = 1729 and yields [0.00, 0.015]; analysis logs and figure artifacts (analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived.

Repair activity and representative diagnostic. The guarded pipeline invoked a single automated repair for one task (stage_counts: repair = 1). The verifier trace for the repaired task shows the shared initial candidate violated the task's required_sequence (a multi-step ordering breach across devices). The repair produced an adjusted command sequence that satisfied ordering constraints and was accepted by the verifier. Representative artifacts for this repaired pair are archived (execution/scoring/task-000008-*.json and execution/responses/task-000008-*.txt). Example normalized configurations and validator snapshots (validation_before/validation_after) are preserved in scoring traces.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to preregistered estimand. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded conditions began from the identical initial candidate; therefore, the experiment isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair. Readers should not extrapolate these results to claims about constrained prompting, guarded prompts as a first-pass intervention, or benefits from independent multi-sample strategies without a different preregistered execution semantics.

Power, discreteness, and interpretive caution. The preregistration targeted detection of ~10–15 percentage-point paired improvements at N = 200 under mid-range baseline expectations (45–65%). The observed baseline pass rate (199/200 = 99.5%) greatly exceeded planning assumptions and consequently reduced realized power to detect small absolute improvements. The discreteness of the discordant-count distribution (n = 1) yields a two-sided exact McNemar p = 1.0 and a narrow bootstrap CI upper bound of 0.015; these artifact-backed statistics reflect high uncertainty when discordant events are rare.

Failure-mode significance and operational intuition. The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering violation, aligning with our preregistered hypothesis that multi-device policy interactions and ordering constraints concentrate risk. In this artifact-grounded run, a single deterministic repair sufficed to correct that localized sequence fault. This suggests bounded guarded repair can be effective for sequence- or order-conformance faults in synthetic settings; it does not imply general effectiveness for semantic misinterpretations, missing dependencies observable only via live telemetry, or adversarially induced contaminations.

Contamination and missingness. Contamination checks were performed deterministically before model calls (token-normalized source deduplication); analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty for flagged episodes. Missingness summary indicates complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. These artifacts support that the confirmatory analysis used the full preregistered sample without post-hoc exclusions.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment measuring the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics for LLM-generated network configurations. In this synthetic deterministic task set with the declared model gpt-5-mini, baseline verifier acceptance was 199/200 and guarded acceptance was 200/200; the single automated repair corrected a multi-device ordering violation. The paired absolute risk difference was 0.005 (95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.015]); exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0 for the observed discordant counts. The artifact-grounded evidence supports a constrained conclusion: verifier-guarded repair can deterministically fix localized ordering faults in this synthetic setting, but broader operational claims require multi-model evaluation, independent first-pass contrasts if those estimands are desired, adversarial contamination testing, larger and more diverse task banks, and live-device validation. All artifacts and analysis outputs supporting these claims are archived and indexed in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the manifest indexing archived artifact paths). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock; humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
